meeting_point: 60 Rowes Wharf, Boston, MA - Behind Boston Harbor Hotel
description:
#Haunted Harbor Ghost Cruise with The Histrionic Academy#

Step aboard Northern Lights, a 1920s-style yacht, for a 90-minute evening cruise that blends Boston Harbor’s history with live, spine-tingling storytelling. In partnership with The Histrionic Academy, two costumed performers guide you past island fortresses and dark waterways, weaving an original script of legends and lore—perfectly timed to the city lights at night.

Hear immersive tales of the Lady in Black at Fort Warren, Nix’s Mate and its pirate gibbet, the Great Molasses Flood, the Ghost Frigate, Peter Rugg “the Storm Breeder,” Captain Green at Fort Independence, Boston Light’s curse, and the Lady of the Maritana. Expect call-and-response narration, atmospheric cues, and a quietly eerie vibe—more candlelit folklore than jump scares.

Settle into indoor lounge seating or step onto the open decks for sweeping skyline views. This is a narrated harbor cruise (we don’t land on the islands); sights vary with weather and navigation.

Good to know

Duration: ~90 minutes; evening departures from Rowes Wharf

Live performers from The Histrionic Academy; original script

Climate-controlled interior and open outer decks; restrooms on board

Light concessions/bar available; dress for cool harbor breezes

A memorable night of history + mystery—for curious locals and brave visitors alike.

highlights:
##Notable sites:

George’s Island (Fort Warren)
Most famous for the ghost of the Lady in Black, said to be the spirit of a woman who tried to rescue her husband from the fort during the Civil War. She was caught, tried as a spy, and executed. Her ghost is said to still haunt the fort.

Spectacle Island
Once used as a trash dump and a quarantine site, it has a history of strange sightings and mysterious lights. Though now a park, its past gives it a reputation for lingering spirits.

Thompson Island
Known for its 19th-century school for orphaned boys, the island has stories of unexplained noises and ghostly figures, especially after dark.

Peddocks Island
Home to the remains of Fort Andrews and abandoned structures, the island is rumored to be haunted by former soldiers and prisoners.

Castle Island (Fort Independence)
Linked to the legend that inspired Edgar Allan Poe’s The Cask of Amontillado. A murder at the fort in the 1800s led to ghost stories that still circulate today.
